nodes.title: About this site
nodes.summary:
This is the documentation home of the **HippoCampusRobotics** lab at TUHH's Institute of
Mechanics and Ocean Engineering. It brings four things into one place: setup guides
(migrated page for page from the old Sphinx sit

nodes.title: Home
nodes.summary: The lab's home for getting robots running: setup guides, every project in one place, searchable code and CAD, and the tools our AI agents use.

nodes.title: Projects
nodes.summary: Everything the lab builds, grouped into projects. One project can own many repositories; forks of upstream software are listed inside the project that uses them.

nodes.title: Agent tools
nodes.summary: MCP servers are small programs that give AI agents real capabilities — renting a GPU, reading a CAD assembly — through a standard interface. These are the lab's tools. Each page will take you from nothing installed to a working agent connection.

nodes.title: Acoustics & DVL
nodes.summary:
Acoustic sensing around the vehicles: the doppler velocity log (DVL) that measures
velocity over ground, and the message definitions for acoustic ranging and modems.

nodes.title: Cameras
nodes.summary:
Image streams into ROS: the MJPEG USB camera driver the vehicles use, and the event-camera
work from a research collaboration.

nodes.title: Core software stack (ROS 2)

definitions that tie nodes together, and the meta packages that pull a full system onto a
robot. If you contribute code to the lab,

nodes.title: Deployment & dev infrastructure
nodes.summary:
How software actually reaches robots and users: deployment configuration for onboard
computers, the bot that builds Debian packages, and the dependency definitions that make
`rosdep` work for lab packages.

nodes.title: Documentation & site
nodes.summary:
The lab's documentation about itself: the current Sphinx docs site, the org website, and
the org profile.

nodes.title: HippoCampus vehicle

robot sized for the institute's tank. This project collects everything that defines the

nodes.title: Localization
nodes.summary:
Knowing where the vehicle is inside the tank. The current approach is visual: cameras on
the vehicle detect AprilTag markers, and an EKF fuses the detections into a pose estimate.

nodes.title: Radio & communications
nodes.summary:
Getting data to and from vehicles without a tether: the HippoLink telemetry link over
Si1000-family radios, the MAVLink plumbing underneath, and software-defined radio
experiments.

nodes.title: Scalar-field exploration
nodes.summary:
Informative path planning over scalar fields — temperature-like quantities spread over the
tank. The vehicle maintains a belief about the field and plans where measuring next helps
most. This is the lab's active research

behave like water (buoyancy, drag, thrusters), and the vehicle models.
